title: Journaling statistics: what the research shows
seoTitle: Journaling statistics: 38 numbers, every one sourced
description: Journaling, worry, sleep, meditation and habit statistics, each checked against the original study: effect sizes, app retention, and what actually helps.
dek: Thirty-eight numbers about writing, worrying, sleeping and starting over, each one traced to the study it came from.

faq.q: What percentage of worries never come true?
faq.a: In two trials of worry outcome journals with people who have generalized anxiety disorder, 91.4% and 89.14% of the feared outcomes did not happen. When they did, people usually coped better than they expected.

Across 146 randomized studies, writing about personal experiences had a real but small average effect (r = .075). A 2023 meta-analysis of 31 trials found a small effect on depression, anxiety and stress that tended to show up weeks later.

faq.q: How many people keep using meditation apps?
faq.a: Few. The median 30-day retention for mindfulness and meditation apps was 4.7% in one analysis of real usage, and fewer than 20% of new Medito users were still meditating after 14 days.

faq.q: How long does it take to form a habit?
faq.a: Between 18 and 254 days in the study behind the famous 66-day average, which came from 39 of 96 volunteers. In a 2021 trial, only 23% of participants reached the threshold for a formed habit within 12 weeks.
